syllabus.clause: AppendEntries{term, prev_log_index, prev_log_term, entries, leader_commit}. An entry commits only once stored on a majority under the leader's current term (the Figure 8 hazard). Conflict repair: the leader backs up to a common prefix and overwrites a follower's divergent suffix, and it must be impossible to silently corrupt indexes. Separating consensus from the state machine lets you test consensus against a trivial KV state machine first.

items.item: a log entry is committed once the leader that created the entry has replicated it on a majority of the servers

at.step: Now a single entry from a previous term already sits on a real majority of the cluster. Does the leader genuinely count it as committed, just from that real majority alone?

items.item: Raft never commits log entries from previous terms by counting replicas; only log entries from the leader's current term are committed by counting replicas

at.step: The Raft paper itself states this exact rule directly, in its own words: only entries from the leader's own current term are ever committed by counting replicas. Does this topic's own code measure exactly that rule?

items.item: the leader handles inconsistencies by forcing the followers' logs to duplicate its own; conflicting entries in follower logs will be overwritten with entries from the leader's log

at.step: A follower's own log genuinely diverges from the leader's at one point. The leader retries AppendEntries, backing up one entry at a time. Does it genuinely find the real common prefix, and overwrite only the divergent suffix?

items.item: to bring a follower's log into consistency, the leader finds the latest log entry where the two logs agree, deletes any entries after that point, and sends the follower all of the leader's entries after that point

items.item: a leader never overwrites or deletes entries in its own log

items.item: The AppendEntries call implemented here carries all five of the syllabus's own named fields (term, prev_log_index, prev_log_term, entries, leader_commit), and every field is genuinely used: term gates a stale leader, prev_log_index and prev_log_term drive the real consistency check, entries are the real payload, and leader_commit genuinely advances the follower's own commit index on success.
